- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.text:
Obico's emails on its Chargebee test site are back to how they were before I changed them. I put each one back by hand from copies of the original text I saved before editing. I didn't find a restore button in Chargebee. Obico's live Chargebee site was never touched.

**What I put back:**
- The logo at the top of every email is the large, centred Obico logo again.
- The sign-off is "Print Smart, – The Obico team" again.
- The line at the bottom of every email is the italic "Obico was previously known as 'The Spaghetti Detective'" again.
- The welcome email for new paid subscriptions has its original heading, body and closing paragraph again, and it's published.
- I deleted the subscription filter "JusPrin 2 plans" that I had created. The extra welcome email I had set up just for that filter was already gone.

**How I checked it:** I created a new JusPrin Hobby subscription for the test customer jusprinv2-mailtest-ob and opened the welcome email it sent in that customer's Email Logs. It's the original Obico email from top to bottom:
- the Obico logo
- "Thank you for supporting Obico!"
- the Detective Hour note
- "Print Smart, – The Obico team"
- the "previously known" line

The email bounced, as all test-site email does: Gmail rejects mail from admin@obico.io that comes from Chargebee's test site because of obico.io's email authentication (DMARC) policy. The preview still shows exactly what would have been sent.

**What I left on the test site:** none of this changes what Obico customers see, but it's clutter.
- **A custom customer field:** called `cf_product`, which I added.
- **Two test customers:** jusprinv2-mailtest-jp and jusprinv2-mailtest-ob, with Hobby subscriptions and three invoices (1070, 1071 and 1072) marked as paid offline.
- **Tags on staging customers:** jusprinv2-490, 491 and 492 have `cf_product` set to jusprin2.

**What's next for the separate JusPrin site:**
- **Your part:** you need to create the JusPrin Chargebee site, both a test site and a live site, because I'm not allowed to create accounts. I couldn't find on Chargebee's pricing page whether a second site can sit under the same account or needs its own plan.
- **Server change, once the site exists:** I'll write it in tsd-enterprise as a proposal and won't push it. JusPrin 2 billing calls would use the new site's API key, and the new site would get its own webhook address.
- **Setting up the new site:** I'll add the Hobby and Workshop plans, the credit pack, the Obico Premium discount coupon, JusPrin branding and JusPrin's own emails.
- **Payments and email to check:** whether the existing Stripe and PayPal accounts can connect to a second Chargebee site, and how to verify jusprin-support@obico.io as the sender.

I've written all of this into `chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md` in the shared notes folder. It replaces the earlier plan to put JusPrin text inside Obico's emails.

Chargebee's docs describe a few ways to get more than one site, depending on whether you want a separate live account or a test environment.

- **Separate sites:** Chargebee says you can have multiple sites, and each one is operated independently from each other and will need to be maintained separately. To create one, you sign up with an email address that isn't tied to an existing site, since a new Chargebee Site/Account needs one.
- **Access from one login:** You can use one primary email address to access all your Chargebee sites by inviting the email address to all the sites you need access to. Logging in as that user then shows all your Chargebee sites, and you can select the one you want to enter.
- **Test sites:** For extra test environments, the sandbox feature applies. You can click + Create new sandbox site from the left navigation, and you can create up to two additional sandboxes per account.
- **Multiple businesses on one site:** If you need several businesses under one site, Multi-Business Entity is the option. By default, you can create up to 3 business entities per Chargebee site. The FAQ also says that if you have multiple live sites in Chargebee, they need to be merged into a single Multi-Business Entity site.

The search results don't say whether the sandbox and multi-entity limits differ by plan. Check the current plans and pricing page or contact Chargebee support before relying on specific limits.

content.content:
**What can differ per business entity**

The article is clear on a few items:
- **Email notifications:** "Each business entity must have its own email notification settings configured separately" (site-level settings don't carry over).
- **Payment gateways:** "A gateway added for one business entity is available only to that entity." Gateways added at the site level are available to all entities.
- **Offline payment methods:** Configurable per entity, per the linked offline payments article.
- **Tax:** Entities use their own organization address and company codes, though tax calculation otherwise follows the customer's billing or shipping country.

The following are set at the site level only:
- **Currencies:** Currencies are limited to the site level.
- **Dunning:** Dunning is limited to the site level.
- **Languages:** "language settings are common across all business entities and can only be configured at the site level"

The article doesn't address branding/logos, invoice templates, hosted checkout pages, the customer portal, or the product catalog per entity. It only notes that the default entity is used in the checkout and portal flow. The article also says entities are "customizable at the entity level," but doesn't list which settings that covers.

**How MBE is enabled**

- **Single live site:** Enable MBE from the settings page. Existing customers move into the first entity. The article describes this as "straightforward."
- **Multiple live sites:** These must be merged into one MBE site. Options include a self-serve route with Chargebee's guidance (contact support for documentation) or having Chargebee's PS&I team do it for a fee. The article notes that you can "raise a request to merge sites by clicking 'Request Support'."

**Plans**

MBE is "available on specific Chargebee plans and pricing," with no plan names listed. Entity limits by Enterprise tier are:
- Enterprise: 3 entities
- Enterprise Tier 1: 30 entities
- Enterprise Tier 2: 100 entities

**Product Catalog 1.0**

The article doesn't address whether MBE is available with Product Catalog 1.0.

**Customer data separation**

Yes, customer data is separated by entity. A customer created under one entity "cannot be linked to any other entity." To serve the same person in two entities, you must create a duplicate customer with a separate ID in each. The article suggests a shared custom field to unify them in RevenueStory.

content.text:
I didn't create anything, because a new Chargebee site turns out to be a new Chargebee account. Chargebee's help page says to "sign up for a new Chargebee site using a different email address" ([multiple sites under one account](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/kb/billing/can-i-create-multiple-sites-under-one-chargebee-account)). I'm not allowed to sign up for accounts on your behalf, even with your yes, so this step has to be yours.

That's also why you couldn't find a button for it. When I opened the site menu in your Chrome, it offered only two things. One was "Create Sandbox", which makes a copy of Obico's site for testing and can never take real payments. The other was the one other site you can reach, called getanywhere. So the sandbox button I offered you isn't really an option for real JusPrin billing.

Chargebee also lets one site hold several businesses, each with its own email settings and payment accounts. That needs an Enterprise plan ([business entity FAQ](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/multi-business-entity/mbe-faq)), so I'd rule it out.

**What to do:**
1. Go to https://www.chargebee.com/trial-signup/ and sign up with an email address that isn't already on a Chargebee site. Your current login is k@thespaghettidetective.com, so use any other address, for example a JusPrin one.
2. Name the site something like "jusprin". Chargebee creates the test site with it, and you switch to the live side later.
3. On the new site, go to Settings › Team Members and invite k@thespaghettidetective.com. After that, your usual login shows a list of all your sites to pick from.
4. Each site is billed separately. Earlier I found a plan at $0 per month plus 0.80% of revenue, so choose that one when Chargebee asks you for a plan.

**What happens next:** once you're signed in to the new test site in Chrome, tell me. From there, I'll do the rest:
- Create the Hobby and Workshop monthly plans, the credit pack and the Obico Premium 20% coupon.
- Turn on one-time checkout and set up the JusPrin branding and emails.
- Write the tsd-enterprise change as a proposal without pushing it. It points JusPrin 2 billing at the new site's API key and gives the new site its own webhook address.
- Ask you before I connect Stripe or PayPal and before anything goes live.

I'm into the new JusPrin Chargebee site, and its catalog now matches the JusPrin 2 items on Obico's test site. In my Chrome your invite showed as "Pending Invite", and I accepted it. Only the test site exists so far, at jusprinv2-test.chargebee.com. Chargebee adds the live site when you activate the account.

**What I created on the test site:**

| What | ID | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Hobby plan | price `jusprin-hobby-monthly` | $10 a month |
| Workshop plan | price `jusprin-workshop-monthly` | $20 a month |
| Credit pack, a one-off charge named "JusPrin Credit Pack (500 credits)" | price `jusprin-credit-pack-USD` | $10 |
| Obico Premium coupon | `jusprin2-obico-premium-20` | 20% off forever, on those two plan prices only |

I opened each one afterwards and checked its ID and price. All of them sit in a product family called "JusPrin". The site also came with Chargebee's sample products, called "OmniSupport Solutions", which I left alone.

**One thing that grows the server work:** the new site uses Chargebee's newer catalog format, version 2.0. Chargebee turns it on for every site created since May 2021 ([product catalog docs](https://chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/product-catalog/product-catalog)), and I found no documented way to switch a new site back. The JusPrin 2 server code is written for the older format. It starts checkouts by plan ID, sells the credit pack as an "addon", and reads `plan_id` from subscriptions in webhooks. On the new site each of those uses a different call or field. So the server change is a port of about a dozen calls in billing.py and the account-deletion view, not just pointing them at a second site.

**Decision needed:** may I create an API key on the new test site? The port can't be tested without one, and creating a key adds a credential to your account, so it's your call.
- **I create it:** I make a full-access key on the test site only and keep it in my local dev setup. I don't put it into staging, and you add it there yourself when the change is ready.
- **You create it:** you make it under Settings › API Keys on jusprinv2-test and put it wherever you want it.

My pick is that I create it, test site only and local only. Until a key exists I can still set up the site's branding and emails, but not the server port.

**Still needs you later:**
- Connecting Stripe or PayPal means signing in to those accounts, so you'll do that or approve it. Until then the test site's built-in test gateway is enough for testing.
- Making jusprin-support@obico.io the sender address means Chargebee sends a verification email to that inbox.

I've written all of this into `chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md` in the shared notes folder.

content.text:
I created the API key on the JusPrin test site, but I couldn't save it anywhere. The key is a full-access key named "claude-local-dev", on jusprinv2-test only. It sits next to the "full_access_key_v1" key Chargebee made when you signed up, which I left untouched.

Claude Code's permission check stopped me from reading the key's value out of the page. Copying a secret into my working context is something it won't allow, and I'm not going to work around that. Without the value saved locally, nothing can use the key yet.

**What you'd do:** copy the claude-local-dev key from Settings › Configure Chargebee › API Keys and Events. Each key has a copy icon next to it. Then run this in a terminal and paste the key when it asks. The key won't show on screen as you paste it.

```bash
read -rs "K?Paste the claude-local-dev key: " && printf 'CHARGEBEE_SITE=jusprinv2-test\nCHARGEBEE_API_KEY=%s\n' "$K" > ~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-test.env && chmod 600 ~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-test.env && unset K
```

This writes the key into `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-test.env`, next to the `prompt-test.env` file you already keep there. Only your user account can read the file.

**What I've set up:** a small script, `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/14cb6590-7113-489e-aa7f-9aa6dca15e79/scratchpad/cbj.sh`, that calls Chargebee with the key from that file and never prints it. It refuses to run unless the site name ends in "-test" and the key starts with "test_", so it can never reach a live site.

**What happens after:** once the file exists, I'll check the key against the site. Then I'll port the JusPrin 2 billing code in tsd-enterprise to the new catalog format and test it against the new test site. That change stays a proposal, and I won't push it.

    """GET: the person's credits, plan and usage, for the composer's balance
    ring and the pre-send check. DELETE: deletes the account, from Delete
    account in the app's Preferences; the app signs out after."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    if request.method == 'DELETE':
        _delete_account(user)
        return HttpResponse(status=204)
    response = JsonResponse(account_summary(user))
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


def _delete_account(user):
    """Ends the plan the account pays for now rather than at the end of its
    term, then deletes the account, and with it its credits, tokens and kept
    chats (jusprin.apps). A JusPrin 2 account is a user of its own, apart from
    the same person's Obico account (lib/syndicate.py), which stays.
    A subscription Chargebee no longer has has nothing left to end. If
    Chargebee can't be reached, nothing is deleted."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan and plan.external_id:
        try:
            status = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(plan.external_id).subscription.status
        except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
            if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
                raise
            status = 'cancelled'
        if status != 'cancelled':
            chargebee.Subscription.cancel(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': False})
    user.delete()

    frame that runs no scripts, so the box is words and pictures only and

    signed_in = 'HTTP_AUTHORIZATION' in request.META

def _delete_account(user):
    """Ends the plan the account pays for now rather than at the end of its
    term, then deletes the account, and with it its credits, tokens and kept
    chats (jusprin.apps). A JusPrin 2 account is a user of its own, apart from
    the same person's Obico account (lib/syndicate.py), which stays.
    A subscription Chargebee no longer has has nothing left to end. If
    Chargebee can't be reached, nothing is deleted."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan and plan.external_id:
        try:
            status = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(plan.external_id).subscription.status
        except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
            if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
                raise
            status = 'cancelled'
        if status != 'cancelled':
            chargebee.Subscription.cancel(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': False})

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:
	•	--no-pager (e.g., git --no-pager log)
	•	or setting GIT_PAGER=cat (e.g., GIT_PAGER=cat git diff)

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.
- Check whether the change could break standalone startup, configuration, or workflows used by self-hosted users. Do not introduce requirements for enterprise-only code, settings, services, or credentials.
- Test affected standalone behavior using `obico-server`'s own configuration and documented setup. Passing tests in the enterprise environment alone does not establish standalone compatibility. If standalone verification cannot be completed, explicitly report what remains unverified and why.

---
name: one-local-server-no-second-stack
description: "tsd-enterprise's local server is the one docker compose stack in the main checkout; never start a second web container, port or database for JusPrin v2 or a branch; branch migrations may run on the normal local DB."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: c868826d-3950-4f0f-9ecd-4a549cdd6983
  modified: 2026-11-03T23:06:20.689Z
---

# Setting up JusPrin 2's host on a server

JusPrin 2 signs in on a host of its own, such as `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` on
staging. Accounts made through that host belong to the `jusprinv2` syndicate,
apart from any Obico account with the same email: the request's host picks the
syndicate (`obico-server/backend/lib/syndicate.py`). Google sign-in on that host
uses JusPrin's own Google client, so Google's sign-in screens are JusPrin's,
not Obico's. Each server needs this set up once, by hand.
`web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/jusprin_host.py` builds the same rows for the tests.

Staging was set up on 2026-11-10. Production has no JusPrin 2 host yet; its
host will be `jusprinv2.obico.io`, which the Google client already accepts as
a redirect address.

## 1. The syndicate and the site

The Django admin doesn't edit syndicates, so run this in a Django shell on the
web pod (`python manage.py shell`), with the host's name:

```python
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from app.models import SiteSyndicate, Syndicate

domain = 'jusprinv2.obico.io'
syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
SiteSyndicate.objects.update_or_create(site=site, defaults={'syndicate': syndicate})
```

It changes nothing when run again.

## 2. Google sign-in

The Google client is "JusPrin 2 server", a Web application client in the
Google Cloud project `jusprin`:

- Client ID: `477983024689-h769gibj38tbs3smov9mci575t0khkbf.apps.googleusercontent.com`
- Redirect addresses: `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`
  and `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`

In the admin, under Social applications, add one:

- Provider: Google
- Name: `JusPrin Google`
- Client id: the client ID above
- Secret key: the client's secret. Google shows a secret only when it is made,
  so take it from wherever it was stored then, or add a new secret on the
  client's page in the Google Cloud console.
- Sites: only JusPrin 2's host.

allauth refuses a site that two Google apps serve, so if another Google app
(Obico's) has JusPrin 2's host ticked, untick it there.

## 3. Check it

Open `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/?process=login`. It should redirect
to `accounts.google.com` with the client ID above and
`redirect_uri=https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/`.

@csrf_exempt
def jusprin_cb_webhook(request):
    """
    Dedicated JustPrint subscription webhook handler

    This is completely decoupled from the Obico webhook system.

    Args:
        request: Django request object with webhook payload

    Returns:
        HttpResponse: Empty response indicating successful processing
    """
    SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS = [
        'subscription_created', 'subscription_started', 'subscription_activated',
        'subscription_changed', 'subscription_cancellation_scheduled',
        'subscription_cancelled', 'subscription_reactivated', 'subscription_renewed'
    ]

    payload = request.body
    cb_event = json.loads(payload)

    # JusPrin 2's plans and credit packs.
    if handle_jusprin_v2_event(cb_event):
        return HttpResponse('')

    if cb_event['event_type'] in SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS:
        cb_sub = cb_event['content']['subscription']

        # Verify this is actually a JusPrin subscription
        if not is_jusprin_subscription(cb_sub['plan_id']):
            return HttpResponse('')  # Ignore non-JustPrint subscriptions

# JusPrin 2 Chargebee and production readiness, checked 2026-11-09

## Chargebee objects (read-only API, both sites on Product Catalog 1.0, USD only)

| Object | Test site (thespaghettidetective-test) | Live site (thespaghettidetective) |
|---|---|---|
| plan jusprin-hobby-monthly | exists, $10/month, invoice name "JusPrin Hobby" | missing |
| plan jusprin-workshop-monthly | exists, $20/month, "JusPrin Workshop" | missing |
| addon jusprin-credit-pack | was missing; created by this session 2026-11-09: $10, non_recurring, invoice name "JusPrin Credit Pack (500 credits)" | missing |
| coupon jusprin2-obico-premium-20 | exists, 20%, forever, only the two plans | missing |
| One-time checkout setting | OFF: hosted_pages/checkout_one_time answers "One time checkout is not enabled under Checkout & Self-Serve Portal" | not checked (no read-only way); assume off |
| Webhook endpoint | app-stg.obico.io/ent/cb_webhook/ (delivers; JusPrin 2 handler runs first) | app.thespaghettidetective.com/ent/cb_webhook/ reaches prod; nothing new needed |

Prices in GET /v2/account match: pack 1000 cents/500 credits, Hobby 1000/750, Workshop 2000/1000.
No yearly JusPrin 2 price ids in the code. Customer ids jusprinv2-<user id> are created on first checkout.
Local docker stack and staging share the test site, so jusprinv2-<id> can collide between them (test-only nuisance).

## Staging runs (accounts k+cb1109-{pack,plan,prem,fail}@obico.io, users 490-493; Obico base user 494 with a fake paid Subscription)

No card was entered anywhere. Payments were simulated with offline payments recorded on the Chargebee test site.

- Guest prices page (?guest=1): right prices, "Sign up to buy".
- Signed-in prices page: right; Premium address shows $10→$8, $20→$16.
- Plan checkout for the Premium address: Chargebee page shows "JusPrin Hobby $10.00 / Obico Premium 20% off -$2.00 / $8.00", Obico logo, a "Remove" link on the coupon.
- Pack checkout: fails ("Checkout couldn't start. Nothing was charged") because of the one-time checkout setting.
- Pack via webhook (invoice 1064 paid): pack 500 + launch_bonus 500, source_ref invoice:1064, once.
- Hobby subscription: 750 + 750 granted at subscription_created **while invoice 1065 was still unpaid** (due_invoices_count 1).
- Hobby→Workshop: Hobby lots expired, Workshop 1000+1000 granted once. Correct.
- Workshop→Hobby same term: Hobby lots stay expired, Workshop's 2000 stay live. Bug.
- Cancel from server billing page: Chargebee non_renewing, billing page "Ends 10 Dec.", but /v2/account still sends renews_at only, so Preferences.tsx:218 shows "Renews 10 Dec.".
- Portal link: redirects to Chargebee portal session. Card line absent (no card on file, expected).
- Not tested: entering a test card, the done page after a real hosted checkout, a failed card, the desktop app UI.

## Emails
- No Chargebee mail reached the k+…@obico.io test addresses. Chargebee docs: a test site mails only the domain it was created with unless support whitelists another.
- Live site mails (BCC to k@obico.io): from "Obico Admin <admin@obico.io>". "Thanks for subscribing" says "THANK YOU FOR SUPPORTING OBICO!", links Detective Hour docs, signed "The Obico team". Failed payment: "[Important] We couldn't charge your Card". JusPrin 2 buyers get these as they are unless templates gain plan-conditional blocks ({{#plan.id = jusprin-hobby-monthly}}) or segmentation (plan-tier dependent).
- "OctoPrint Anywhere <admin@thespaghettidetective.com>" mails come from another Chargebee site (getanywhere), unrelated.
- Live "[Chargebee] Webhook failure" mails come from Sentry OBICO-SERVER-AS7 (User.DoesNotExist in Obico's email path, since 2026-08-12), not JusPrin 2.
- Sentry OBICO-SERVER-B22 (JSONDecodeError at /ent/cb_webhook/, 2026-11-10 02:46 UTC) was this session's HEAD probe of the prod webhook URL. Harmless; resolve it.

## Production settings vs staging
- tsdweb-prod/tsdws-prod run obi.4088; staging obi.4096. 4088 lacks JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION, sign-in mail from jusprin-support@obico.io, host-based brands.
- ConfigMap jusprin-v2-gateway-prod is the old shape: obi.4088 itself rejects it ("alias is missing ['credits', 'tier']"). No slicer-basic alias. Staging's has both.
- tsdws-prod lacks JUSPRIN_OPENROUTER_API_KEY (staging has it; needed by slicer-basic).
- Prod DB: no jusprinv2 syndicate, no jusprinv2.obico.io Site. DNS for jusprinv2.obico.io does not resolve. No prod managed cert or ingress rule. All covered by ops tsd/RUNBOOK.md "JusPrin's host".
- JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION blank on both. JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER blank on both (chats are not kept).
- Other web env names identical between stg and prod.

## Proposed server fix (not applied, not tested)
proposed-billing-fix.patch in this folder: grant a term only when the subscription has no unpaid invoices, grant it on payment_succeeded otherwise, and reopen a plan's lots on a switch back. Separately /v2/account needs an "ends" signal (plan.expired_at) and Preferences.tsx needs "Ends <day>." when set.

- Hobby subscription: 750 + 750 granted at subscription_created **while invoice 1065 was still unpaid** (due_invoices_count 1).
- Hobby→Workshop: Hobby lots expired, Workshop 1000+1000 granted once. Correct.
- Workshop→Hobby same term: Hobby lots stay expired, Workshop's 2000 stay live. Bug.
- Cancel from server billing page: Chargebee non_renewing, billing page "Ends 10 Dec.", but /v2/account still sends renews_at only, so Preferences.tsx:218 shows "Renews 10 Dec.".
- Portal link: redirects to Chargebee portal session. Card line absent (no card on file, expected).
- Not tested: entering a test card, the done page after a real hosted checkout, a failed card, the desktop app UI.

## Emails
- No Chargebee mail reached the k+…@obico.io test addresses. Chargebee docs: a test site mails only the domain it was created with unless support whitelists another.
- Live site mails (BCC to k@obico.io): from "Obico Admin <admin@obico.io>". "Thanks for subscribing" says "THANK YOU FOR SUPPORTING OBICO!", links Detective Hour docs, signed "The Obico team". Failed payment: "[Important] We couldn't charge your Card". JusPrin 2 buyers get these as they are unless templates gain plan-conditional blocks ({{#plan.id = jusprin-hobby-monthly}}) or segmentation (plan-tier dependent).
- "OctoPrint Anywhere <admin@thespaghettidetective.com>" mails come from another Chargebee site (getanywhere), unrelated.
- Live "[Chargebee] Webhook failure" mails come from Sentry OBICO-SERVER-AS7 (User.DoesNotExist in Obico's email path, since 2026-08-12), not JusPrin 2.
- Sentry OBICO-SERVER-B22 (JSONDecodeError at /ent/cb_webhook/, 2026-11-10 02:46 UTC) was this session's HEAD probe of the prod webhook URL. Harmless; resolve it.

## Production settings vs staging
- tsdweb-prod/tsdws-prod run obi.4088; staging obi.4096. 4088 lacks JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION, sign-in mail from jusprin-support@obico.io, host-based brands.

- tsdws-prod lacks JUSPRIN_OPENROUTER_API_KEY (staging has it; needed by slicer-basic).
- Prod DB: no jusprinv2 syndicate, no jusprinv2.obico.io Site. DNS for jusprinv2.obico.io does not resolve. No prod managed cert or ingress rule. All covered by ops tsd/RUNBOOK.md "JusPrin's host".
- JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION blank on both. JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER blank on both (chats are not kept).
- Other web env names identical between stg and prod.

## Proposed server fix (not applied, not tested)
proposed-billing-fix.patch in this folder: grant a term only when the subscription has no unpaid invoices, grant it on payment_succeeded otherwise, and reopen a plan's lots on a switch back. Separately /v2/account needs an "ends" signal (plan.expired_at) and Preferences.tsx needs "Ends <day>." when set.

"""DELETE /ent/jusprin/v2/account: ends a paid plan in Chargebee now, then
deletes the account; if Chargebee fails, nothing is deleted."""
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest import mock

import chargebee
from django.test import Client, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application

from app.models import User
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import ensure_lots
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditGrant
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/account'


def chargebee_says(status):
    return SimpleNamespace(subscription=SimpleNamespace(status=status))


@mock.patch('jusprin.v2.views.chargebee.Subscription')
class AccountDeleteTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'delete-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def delete(self, token=None):
        return Client().delete(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token or self.token}')

    def plan(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-workshop-monthly', external_id='sub_1',
                                   external_user_id='cus_1')

    def gone(self):
        return not User.objects.filter(id=self.user.id).exists()

    def test_needs_a_token(self, subscription):
        self.assertEqual(Client().delete(URL).status_code, 401)
        self.assertEqual(self.delete('not-a-token').status_code, 401)
        self.assertFalse(self.gone())

    def test_an_account_without_a_plan_is_deleted_with_its_credits_and_tokens(self, subscription):
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())
        self.assertFalse(CreditGrant.objects.filter(user_id=self.user.id).exists())
        self.assertFalse(AccessToken.objects.filter(token=self.token).exists())
        subscription.retrieve.assert_not_called()
        self.assertEqual(Client().get(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}').status_code, 401)

    def test_a_plan_ends_now_not_at_the_end_of_its_term(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.return_value = chargebee_says('active')
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel.assert_called_once_with('sub_1', {'end_of_term': False})
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())
        self.assertFalse(JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=self.user.id).exists())

    def test_a_plan_chargebee_already_cancelled_is_not_cancelled_again(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.return_value = chargebee_says('cancelled')
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel.assert_not_called()
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())

    def test_a_plan_chargebee_no_longer_has_is_not_cancelled(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.side_effect = chargebee.InvalidRequestError(
            404, {'message': "Sorry, we couldn't find that resource", 'type': 'invalid_request',
             'api_error_code': 'resource_not_found', 'error_code': 'resource_not_found'})
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel.assert_not_called()
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())

    def test_if_chargebee_fails_the_account_stays(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.return_value = chargebee_says('active')
        subscription.cancel.side_effect = RuntimeError('Chargebee is down')
        client = Client(raise_request_exception=False)
        self.assertEqual(client.delete(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}').status_code, 500)
        self.assertFalse(self.gone())

    def test_other_methods_are_refused(self, subscription):
        response = Client().post(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}')
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 405)
        self.assertFalse(self.gone())

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`
