tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. content.text:
The PayPal test checkout on the JusPrin test site is waiting for you to sign in as the sandbox buyer. I can't type passwords, so this step is yours.

The first try didn't work because Chrome was still signed in to the PayPal sandbox as the shop's own account (k-facilitator@getanywhere.io). PayPal won't let the shop pay itself. I signed that account out and started the payment again.

A PayPal tab titled "Log in to your PayPal account" is now open in Chrome. In that tab:
1. Sign in as **k-buyer@getanywhere.io**. Its password is on the PayPal developer dashboard, which is the other open tab, under Sandbox accounts.
2. Approve the $10 JusPrin Hobby payment.

After you approve, I'll check that a test user received the Hobby plan's credits and that PayPal took the payment.

#!/bin/bash
# Chargebee API helper for the JusPrin test site. Reads the key from a file
# Kenneth writes; never prints it. Usage: ./cbj.sh METHOD PATH [curl args]
set -euo pipefail
F="$HOME/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-test.env"
KEY=$(sed -n "s/^CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=//p" "$F" | tr -d "'\" ")
SITE=$(sed -n "s/^CHARGEBEE_SITE=//p" "$F" | tr -d "'\" ")
[[ "$SITE" == *-test ]] || { echo "refusing non-test site: $SITE" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ "$KEY" == test_* ]] || { echo "key in $F is not a test key" >&2; exit 1; }
M=$1; P=$2; shift 2
curl -sS -X "$M" -u REDACTED "https://$SITE.chargebee.com/api/v2/$P" "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# Chargebee API helper for the JusPrin test site. Reads the key from a file
# Kenneth writes; never prints it. Usage: ./cbj.sh METHOD PATH [curl args]
set -euo pipefail
F="$HOME/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-test.env"
KEY=$(sed -n "s/^CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=//p" "$F" | tr -d "'\" ")
SITE=$(sed -n "s/^CHARGEBEE_SITE=//p" "$F" | tr -d "'\" ")
[[ "$SITE" == *-test ]] || { echo "refusing non-test site: $SITE" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ "$KEY" == test_* ]] || { echo "key in $F is not a test key" >&2; exit 1; }
M=$1; P=$2; shift 2
curl -sS -X "$M" -u REDACTED "https://$SITE.chargebee.com/api/v2/$P" "$@"

content.text:
Both payment methods now work on JusPrin's test Chargebee site. Your PayPal approval completed a $10 Hobby plan purchase. PayPal took the money, Chargebee started the subscription, and our server gave the test user the plan's credits.

**What I checked after you approved:**
- **In Chargebee:**
  - The Hobby subscription is active.
  - The $10.00 payment went through the test site's PayPal connection.
  - The buyer's PayPal account is saved as a valid payment method, with automatic charging on, so next month's renewal can charge it without the buyer.
- **On the local server:**
  - Recording the checkout gave the test user 750 Hobby credits plus the 750 double-credits launch bonus, both expiring 10 Dec.
  - With the 500 sign-up credits, the account shows 2,000.
  - The account reply says the plan renews on 10 Dec.
- **Stripe:** a card checkout through Stripe passed earlier.

The PayPal error you hit had a simple cause. Chrome kept filling the sign-in page with the shop's own sandbox email, and PayPal won't let a shop pay itself. Using the buyer's email fixed it.

**What's left before real customers can pay on JusPrin's live Chargebee site:**
1. **You turn on the live site.** None of the test setup carries over; Chargebee says each payment method must be connected again on the live site.
2. **Connect Stripe and PayPal on the live site** to the same TSD Technology accounts. Card statements will read "OBICO/THE SPAGHETTI DE" unless you change the statement name in Stripe.
3. **PayPal recurring payments.** Chargebee warns that a PayPal setting called "Reference Transactions" must be on for monthly renewals to charge. The sandbox worked without me changing anything. I haven't checked the live TSD PayPal account. If Obico's live site already renews subscriptions through that account, it's probably on.
4. **The server's Chargebee webhook** must be added on the live site, the same way as on the test site.
5. **Staging**, when you want it there, needs its own test-site API key. You approved the current key for local development only.
6. **Still open from before:** the site's look and logo, verifying the address emails are sent from, and what happens to JusPrin 1 subscribers' coupons.

I've added the gateway setup and the PayPal sign-in trap to the shared notes file, chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md. Nothing is pushed, and I changed nothing in production.

content.text:
No to both. I haven't tested on staging at all, so we're not ready for production.

**What has been tested:** everything ran on my local server against JusPrin's test Chargebee site, including:
- a credit pack purchase,
- Hobby and Workshop plans paid by card through Stripe and by PayPal,
- plan switches, a payment that hadn't gone through yet, and a cancel.

**Why staging isn't ready:**
- The server code is committed only on a local tsd-enterprise branch (jusprin-v2-own-chargebee-site, two commits). It has never been pushed, so staging doesn't run it.
- The staging and production settings files I copied on 9 Nov have no JusPrin 2 Chargebee settings.
- You approved the test-site API key for local development only, so staging would need its own test-site key.
- The app change that shows "Ends 10 Dec." after a plan is cancelled is also committed locally only, on its own JusPrin branch.

**Putting it on staging would take five steps:**
1. Push the server branch to tsd-enterprise master and deploy staging.
2. You create a second API key on the test Chargebee site for staging.
3. Put that key and the site name into staging's settings.
4. Point the test site's webhook at staging, so Chargebee's payment notices reach the staging server.
5. Then I'd repeat the purchases there (pack, plan by card, plan by PayPal) and check the credits in the app connected to staging.

**Production needs everything above, plus:**
- You turn on JusPrin's live Chargebee site.
- Stripe and PayPal are connected again on the live site, to the same TSD accounts.
- Someone checks that PayPal's "Reference Transactions" setting is on for the live TSD PayPal account, or monthly renewals can't charge.
- The production server gets the live API key, and the live site gets its webhook.
- The items still open from before: the site's look and logo, verifying the address emails come from, and what happens to JusPrin 1 subscribers' coupons.

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:
	•	--no-pager (e.g., git --no-pager log)
	•	or setting GIT_PAGER=cat (e.g., GIT_PAGER=cat git diff)

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.
- Check whether the change could break standalone startup, configuration, or workflows used by self-hosted users. Do not introduce requirements for enterprise-only code, settings, services, or credentials.
- Test affected standalone behavior using `obico-server`'s own configuration and documented setup. Passing tests in the enterprise environment alone does not establish standalone compatibility. If standalone verification cannot be completed, explicitly report what remains unverified and why.

#!/bin/bash -e

RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Trap to catch errors and display in red
trap 'exit_code=$?; trap - ERR; echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Command failed with exit code $exit_code${NC}" >&2; exit $exit_code' ERR

. $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh

# ── Preflight checks ──

echo "Running preflight checks..."

# Ensure obico-server is on master and push
cd obico-server
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! obico-server is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing obico-server..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push obico-server. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
cd ..

# Ensure tsd-enterprise is on master and push
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! tsd-enterprise is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing tsd-enterprise..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push tsd-enterprise. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Preflight checks passed ✅"

# ── Build ──

cd obico-server/frontend
nvm use
npm ci # for some reason if node_modules folder is missing in the public repo, `npm run build` in the ent repo will fail

if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
git pull && git checkout master
LAST_PUB_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"
git push

cd ../..
if git diff-index HEAD -- | grep -v obico-server ; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1

#!/bin/bash -e

for f in tsdweb-stg.yaml tsdtasks-stg.yaml tsdws-stg.yaml tsdbeat-stg.yaml
do
    kubectl --context=tsd apply -f $f
    sleep 5
    kubectl --context=tsd get pods --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o wide
done

#!/bin/bash -e

for file in ./*-stg.yaml; do
    [ -f "$file" ] && sed -i '' -e "s|image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$1|image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$2|g" "$file"
done

count=$(grep -l "image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$2" ./*-stg.yaml 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "stg:     $count"


for file in ../prod/*-prod.yaml; do
    [ -f "$file" ] && sed -i '' -e "s|image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$1|image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$2|g" "$file"
done

count=$(grep -l "image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.$2" ../prod/*-prod.yaml 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "prod:    $count"
The gateway's two streaming paths, `/ent/jusprin/v2/messages` and
`/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`, go to the websocket service (daphne), not the web
service: they stream for minutes, and gunicorn's sync workers cannot stream
them. The rest of `/ent/jusprin/v2/`, including `/models`, stays on the web
service. Both deployments read the gateway's alias config from a ConfigMap
(`jusprin-v2-gateway-<env>.yaml`) and the upstream keys from a Secret of the
same name that is created with kubectl and is not in this repo; restart both
deployments after changing either.

The path rules exist on every staging and production app host
(`app-stg.*` to `tsdws-stg-svc`; `app.obico.io`, `app.thespaghettidetective.com`
and `app.kingroon.com` to `tsdws-prod-svc`). The gateway shipped in the normal
release `obi.4048` (2026-10-25), so `stg/update-version.sh` covers both
environments again.

**JusPrin's host: `jusprinv2.obico.io` (staging `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io`).**
Decided 2026-11-04; named `jusprinv2` to keep it apart from JusPrin v1. JusPrin 2 is a syndicate of its own (`jusprinv2`, with its own brand in `SYNDICATES`; the `jusprin` brand is v1's), with its own accounts,
and the server takes a request's syndicate from its host. The desktop app's
browser sign-in runs in the system browser, which cannot send the
`X-Obico-Syndicate` header, so only a host of its own keeps JusPrin sign-ins
apart from Obico's. A separate host also gets its own login cookie (the server
sets no cookie domain), so an Obico website session cannot authorize JusPrin.
Rolling it out, staging first:

1. DNS (Namecheap, obico.io): A records `jusprinv2-stg` and `jusprinv2` to the
   ingress's static IP, the one `app-stg.obico.io` and `app.obico.io` resolve
   to.
2. `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/jusprin-managed-cert.yaml`, then
   `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/neg-ingress.yaml` (the ingress names the
   certificate, so the certificate goes first). A certificate is issued once
   its name resolves to the ingress. Both hosts are in the files:
   `gke-managed-cert-jusprinv2-app` serves `jusprinv2.obico.io`, and its rule
   routes like `app.obico.io`'s.
3. On the server, first move the syndicate id sequence past the existing
   rows: base and kingroon were inserted with explicit ids, so on 2026-11-04
   staging's next id was 2 (kingroon's) and production's 1 (base's). In
   `python manage.py shell` on a web pod:
   `from django.core.management.color import no_style; from django.db import connection; from app.models import Syndicate; [connection.cursor().execute(s) for s in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate])]`
   (done on staging 2026-11-04 and production 2026-11-10). Without it the
   next step fails and rolls back. Then:
   `run_django_mgmt_cmd.sh set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io`
   (production: `jusprinv2.obico.io --google-from app.obico.io`). It makes the
   `jusprinv2` syndicate and the site for the host, takes the site out of the
   base syndicate that a new site joins automatically, and puts Obico's Google
   sign-in app on it. Safe to run again.
4. Google Cloud console, the OAuth client of that Google sign-in app: add
   `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/` as a redirect URI.
5. The desktop app's default gateway (`ProviderProfile.hpp` in JusPrin, the
   "jusprin" row) is `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`. To
   test against staging, set `jusprin_server/base_url` to
   `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` in the app's settings file.

JusPrin v1 users signed in with Obico accounts on `app.obico.io`. The v1 import
leaves that sign-in behind, they sign up again on JusPrin's host, and their
v1 subscriptions are moved to the new accounts by hand
(`jusprin_subscription_status` lists both accounts of an address).

config.yml
version: 2.1
jobs:
  build_web_ent:
    machine:
      image: default
    environment:
      VERSION: << pipeline.number >>
    steps:
      - run: docker login -u $DOCKER_USER -p $DOCKER_PASS

      - checkout
      - run:
          name: "Pull Submodules"
          command: |
            git submodule init
            git submodule update --remote
      # Set up multi-arch build
      - run:
          name: "Set up Docker Buildx"
          command: |
            docker run --rm --privileged multiarch/qemu-user-static --reset -p yes
            docker buildx create --name multiarch --use
            docker buildx inspect --bootstrap
      # build and deploy the application image for multiple architectures
      - run:
          name: "Build and push multi-arch image"
          command: |
            docker buildx build \
              --build-arg VERSION=${VERSION} \
              --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
              -t kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.${VERSION} \
              -f web_ent/Dockerfile \
              --push .

  # build and deploy the ml_api image. The build may take long time. Do it after the web_ent image so the other part of the
  build_ml_api_ent:
    machine:
      image: default
    environment:
      VERSION: << pipeline.number >>
    steps:
      - run: docker login -u $DOCKER_USER -p $DOCKER_PASS

      - checkout
      - run:
          name: "Install git-lfs"
          command: |
            curl -s https://packagecloud.io/install/repositories/github/git-lfs/script.deb.sh | sudo bash
            sudo apt-get install -y git-lfs
            git lfs install
      - run:
          name: "Pull submodules"
          command: |
            git submodule init
            git submodule update --remote
            cd ml_api_ent/first_layer/model/dinov2-small
            git lfs pull

      - run: docker build --build-arg VERSION=${VERSION} -t kennethjiang/ml_api_ent:obi.${VERSION} -f ml_api_ent/Dockerfile .
      - run: docker push kennethjiang/ml_api_ent:obi.${VERSION}

  sentry:
    docker:
      - image: kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.<< pipeline.number >>
    environment:
      SENTRY_ORG: sentry
      SENTRY_PROJECT: obico-frontend
      SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT: production
    working_directory: /app
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Create release and notify Sentry of deploy
          # https://gist.github.com/so0k/3f0546be5f06431a55a0a90ac9c25da8
          command: |
            apk update
            apk upgrade
            apk add curl
            curl -sL https://sentry.io/get-cli/ | bash
            sentry-cli --url https://sentry.obico.io/  releases new -p $SENTRY_PROJECT $VERSION
            sentry-cli --url https://sentry.obico.io/ sourcemaps upload static_build/frontend/js --release ${VERSION} --url-prefix '~/static/frontend/js'

## 3. Chargebee

JusPrin 2 sells credit packs and plans on a Chargebee site of its own,
`jusprinv2`, not on Obico's. Its test site is `jusprinv2-test`, which local
servers and staging use. Both sites use Chargebee's Product Catalog 2.0
(`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py` says what that changes).

Set these on the web pods:

- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE`: `jusprinv2-test` on staging, `jusprinv2` on
  production.
- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`: a full-access API key of that site.

The site's product catalog needs these ids, which the server names in
`settings_ent.py`:

- Plan item prices `jusprin-hobby-monthly` ($10 a month) and
  `jusprin-workshop-monthly` ($20 a month).
- Charge item price `jusprin-credit-pack-USD` ($10), the credit pack.
- Coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20`, 20% off forever, for the two plans only.

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Checkout & Self-Serve Portal ›
Configuration:

- Checkout: turn off "Allow customers to edit quantity for plans", and turn on
  "Allow customers to add/remove coupons".
- Checkout: One time payments: leave it enabled; the credit pack is bought
  through it.
- Self-Serve Portal: set "Customers can access the self-serve portal" to
  "Via Single Sign On API". Otherwise Chargebee refuses the server's portal
  link with "Customer portal access via API is disabled".

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Webhooks, add
`https://<server>/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`, where `<server>` is the server's
own host (`app-stg.obico.io` on staging). The server trusts a post only for
the event's id and reads the event back from the site with its key, so the
webhook needs no password.

## 4. Check it

Open `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/?process=login`. It should redirect
to `accounts.google.com` with the client ID above and
`redirect_uri=https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/`.

Signed in on the host, open `https://<host>/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices` and
start a credit-pack checkout. It should open a `jusprinv2` (or
`jusprinv2-test`) checkout page for $10. On the test site, pay with
Chargebee's test card 4111 1111 1111 1111; the account should gain 500
credits, plus the launch bonus while that offer runs.

The server changes are on tsd-enterprise master as commit 2d97f4b1c7. They're the Chargebee port and the three billing fixes. I moved them onto the current master first: another session had rewritten the Google sign-in commits my branch was built on. All 287 server tests pass on the result.

I also pushed a release commit, e1c059176f, to the release branch, so CircleCI is building the new server image now. The release reuses the last release's website bundles, because nothing in the website's frontend has changed since then.

**What I need from you:** a second API key on JusPrin's test Chargebee site, for staging only.
1. Open jusprinv2-test.chargebee.com → Settings → Configure Chargebee → API Keys and Webhooks → API Keys.
2. Add a **Full-Access** key and name it "staging".
3. Save it in a new file, `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-stg.env`, as one line: `CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=<the key>`

**What I'll do once the key is saved and the image is built:**
- Add the test site's name and that key to staging's web server settings in the ops repo (`tsd/stg/tsdweb-stg.yaml`). The key goes in written out, the same way Obico's test-site key is in that file today.
- Switch staging to the new image and deploy it.
- Add the test site's webhook, `https://app-stg.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`. The test site has no webhooks yet.
- Buy a credit pack and a plan on jusprinv2-stg.obico.io, then check the credits in the app connected to staging.

**Two things you should know before production:**
- **Releasing master now breaks production checkout until production gets its settings.** Master now expects JusPrin's own Chargebee site. If anyone releases master to production before the live site's name and key are in production's settings, JusPrin 2's credit pack and plan checkouts there will fail. Nobody has bought anything through them on production yet.
- **The ops repo has an unpushed commit from another session.** It's 3f5e1b7, about keeping JusPrin 2 chats on staging and production. When I deploy staging, I'll compare the staging file against what's running before applying it, so I don't roll out that session's change by accident.

content.text:
I set the statement text "JUSPRIN" on JusPrin's test Chargebee site and made one test payment by card and one by PayPal. A JusPrin card payment now shows **"OBICO* JUSPRIN"** on the customer's statement. I couldn't confirm what a PayPal statement shows. I changed nothing on Obico's live site, Stripe or PayPal.

**What the test showed:**
- **Stripe card payment:** $10 on a Stripe test card. Stripe records the statement text as "OBICO* JUSPRIN". The test payment made before the setting read "OBICO/THE SPAGHETTI DE". The "OBICO" part is the Stripe account's short name, so it appears on JusPrin charges too.
- **PayPal payment:** $10 charged to the sandbox buyer's saved PayPal account, and it went through. PayPal's sandbox doesn't report a statement line, so what a PayPal statement would show is unverified. The charge also showed that Chargebee can charge a saved PayPal account with nobody present, which is what monthly renewals need.

**What customers see today:**

| | Obico (live) | JusPrin (test site) |
|---|---|---|
| Card statement | "OBICO/THE SPAGHETTI DE" (confirmed on a real charge from today) | "OBICO* JUSPRIN" |
| Business details on invoices | "Obico", 1790 Willow Lake Ln, San Jose CA 95131, +1 (404) 565-4264 | None: no name, logo or address |
| Email sender | "Obico Admin <admin@obico.io>" | Not set up yet |
| PayPal connection | PayPal Express Checkout (the older kind) | PayPal Commerce Platform |

Both sites take payments through the same TSD Stripe account. Stripe's public details are:
- business name "Obico/The Spaghetti Detective"
- support email admin@obico.io
- support phone +1 (408) 889-3920

**Not read:** the live PayPal account's business name and its statement name. paypal.com asked for your sign-in. On PayPal's approval screen, buyers see the shop's PayPal business name; in the sandbox that read "test facilitator's Test Store". So JusPrin and Obico buyers will both see TSD's PayPal business name, whatever it is.

I sent these results back to the session that asked, and added them to the shared notes file chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md.

**Staging** is still waiting on two things:
- **The new server image:** CircleCI has been building it since 19:38 UTC, and I'm watching for it in the background.
- **The staging API key:** from you, as described before. Create a Full-Access key named "staging" on jusprinv2-test.chargebee.com, then save it as `CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=<the key>` in `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-stg.env`.

PY
echo "added"
EOF

CircleCI has built the new server image, obi.4102, and the staging files now name it. Staging itself still runs the old image, obi.4098. The deploy is waiting only on the staging API key for JusPrin's test Chargebee site.

**What I prepared:**
- **Image switch.** The four staging files in the ops repo (web, websocket, tasks, beat) now name obi.4102. I changed only the staging files; the repo's usual version script also edits production's files.
- **What applying will change.** I compared those files with what staging runs now. Apart from the new image, applying them changes nothing. The only other difference is one setting listed in a different order.
- **Settings script.** Only the web pods talk to JusPrin's Chargebee site, so only those get the new settings. A script is ready to add the test-site name and your key to the staging web file. It reads the key straight from your file without printing it, and refuses anything that isn't a test-site key.

**What you need to do:**
1. On jusprinv2-test.chargebee.com, add a Full-Access API key named "staging".
2. Save it in `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-stg.env` as one line: `CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=<the key>`

**Once the key is saved, I'll:**
1. Add it to the staging web file.
2. Deploy staging.
3. Add the test site's webhook for staging.
4. Buy a credit pack and a plan on jusprinv2-stg.obico.io and check the credits.

# Setting up JusPrin 2's host on a server

JusPrin 2 signs in on a host of its own, such as `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` on
staging. Accounts made through that host belong to the `jusprinv2` syndicate,
apart from any Obico account with the same email: the request's host picks the
syndicate (`obico-server/backend/lib/syndicate.py`). Google sign-in on that host
uses JusPrin's own Google client, so Google's sign-in screens are JusPrin's,
not Obico's. Each server needs this set up once, by hand.
`web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/jusprin_host.py` builds the same rows for the tests.

Staging was set up on 2026-11-10. Production has no JusPrin 2 host yet; its
host will be `jusprinv2.obico.io`, which the Google client already accepts as
a redirect address. Neither server has JusPrin 2's own Chargebee site
(section 3) yet.

## 1. The syndicate and the site

The Django admin doesn't edit syndicates, so run this in a Django shell on the
web pod (`python manage.py shell`), with the host's name:

```python
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from app.models import SiteSyndicate, Syndicate

domain = 'jusprinv2.obico.io'
syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
SiteSyndicate.objects.update_or_create(site=site, defaults={'syndicate': syndicate})
```

It changes nothing when run again.

## 2. Google sign-in

The Google client is "JusPrin 2 server", a Web application client in the
Google Cloud project `jusprin`:

- Client ID: `477983024689-h769gibj38tbs3smov9mci575t0khkbf.apps.googleusercontent.com`
- Redirect addresses: `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`
  and `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`

In the admin, under Social applications, add one:

- Provider: Google
- Name: `JusPrin Google`
- Client id: the client ID above
- Secret key: the client's secret. Google shows a secret only when it is made,
  so take it from wherever it was stored then, or add a new secret on the
  client's page in the Google Cloud console.
- Sites: only JusPrin 2's host.

allauth refuses a site that two Google apps serve, so if another Google app
(Obico's) has JusPrin 2's host ticked, untick it there.

## 3. Chargebee

JusPrin 2 sells credit packs and plans on a Chargebee site of its own,
`jusprinv2`, not on Obico's. Its test site is `jusprinv2-test`, which local
servers and staging use. Both sites use Chargebee's Product Catalog 2.0
(`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py` says what that changes).

Set these on the web pods:

- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE`: `jusprinv2-test` on staging, `jusprinv2` on
  production.
- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`: a full-access API key of that site.

The site's product catalog needs these ids, which the server names in
`settings_ent.py`:

- Plan item prices `jusprin-hobby-monthly` ($10 a month) and
  `jusprin-workshop-monthly` ($20 a month).
- Charge item price `jusprin-credit-pack-USD` ($10), the credit pack.
- Coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20`, 20% off forever, for the two plans only.

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Checkout & Self-Serve Portal ›
Configuration:

- Checkout: turn off "Allow customers to edit quantity for plans", and turn on
  "Allow customers to add/remove coupons".
- Checkout: One time payments: leave it enabled; the credit pack is bought
  through it.
- Self-Serve Portal: set "Customers can access the self-serve portal" to
  "Via Single Sign On API". Otherwise Chargebee refuses the server's portal
  link with "Customer portal access via API is disabled".

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Webhooks, add
`https://<server>/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`, where `<server>` is the server's
own host (`app-stg.obico.io` on staging). The server trusts a post only for
the event's id and reads the event back from the site with its key, so the
webhook needs no password.

## 4. Check it

Open `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/?process=login`. It should redirect
to `accounts.google.com` with the client ID above and
`redirect_uri=https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/`.

Signed in on the host, open `https://<host>/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices` and
start a credit-pack checkout. It should open a `jusprinv2` (or
`jusprinv2-test`) checkout page for $10. On the test site, pay with
Chargebee's test card 4111 1111 1111 1111; the account should gain 500
credits, plus the launch bonus while that offer runs.

import django,os,secrets,json; os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE','config.settings'); django.setup()
from datetime import timedelta
from django.utils import timezone
from app.models import User, Syndicate
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application
from app_ent.models import Subscription
tag = os.environ.get('TAG', 'cb1109')
v2 = Syndicate.objects.get(name='jusprinv2'); base = Syndicate.objects.get(name='base')
app = Application.objects.get(client_id='JusPrin2')
def mk(email, synd):
    u = User.objects.filter(email__iexact=email, syndicate=synd).first()
    if u is None:
        u = User(email=email, syndicate=synd, first_name='CB', last_name='Test'); u.set_unusable_password(); u.save()
        EmailAddress.objects.create(user=u, email=email, verified=True, primary=True)
    return u
out = {}
for name in ['pack', 'plan', 'prem', 'fail']:
    email = f'k+{tag}-{name}@obico.io'
    u = mk(email, v2)
    tok = secrets.token_urlsafe(30)
    AccessToken.objects.create(user=u, application=app, token=tok, expires=timezone.now()+timedelta(days=2), scope='read write')
    out[name] = {'id': u.id, 'email': email, 'token': tok}
# The Obico account with a paid subscription under the "prem" address.
ob = mk(out['prem']['email'], base)
Subscription.objects.update_or_create(user=ob, defaults={'external_id': f'stgtest-{tag}', 'external_user_id': f'stgtest-{tag}',
    'plan_id': 'pro-monthly', 'printers_subscribed': 1, 'expired_at': None})
out['prem_obico_user'] = ob.id
print(json.dumps(out))

import django,os,secrets,json; os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE','config.settings'); django.setup()
from datetime import timedelta
from django.utils import timezone
from app.models import User, Syndicate
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application
from app_ent.models import Subscription
tag = os.environ.get('TAG', 'cb1109')
v2 = Syndicate.objects.get(name='jusprinv2'); base = Syndicate.objects.get(name='base')
app = Application.objects.get(client_id='JusPrin2')
def mk(email, synd):
    u = User.objects.filter(email__iexact=email, syndicate=synd).first()
    if u is None:
        u = User(email=email, syndicate=synd, first_name='CB', last_name='Test'); u.set_unusable_password(); u.save()
        EmailAddress.objects.create(user=u, email=email, verified=True, primary=True)
    return u
out = {}
for name in ['pack', 'plan', 'prem', 'fail']:
    email = f'k+{tag}-{name}@obico.io'
    u = mk(email, v2)
    tok = secrets.token_urlsafe(30)
    AccessToken.objects.create(user=u, application=app, token=tok, expires=timezone.now()+timedelta(days=2), scope='read write')
    out[name] = {'id': u.id, 'email': email, 'token': tok}
# The Obico account with a paid subscription under the "prem" address.
ob = mk(out['prem']['email'], base)
Subscription.objects.update_or_create(user=ob, defaults={'external_id': f'stgtest-{tag}', 'external_user_id': f'stgtest-{tag}',
    'plan_id': 'pro-monthly', 'printers_subscribed': 1, 'expired_at': None})
out['prem_obico_user'] = ob.id
print(json.dumps(out))

content.text:
Staging is done and passes. jusprinv2-stg.obico.io now sells JusPrin 2 credits and plans through JusPrin's own test Chargebee site. In Chrome, I bought a credit pack and a Hobby plan, checked the Premium discount, and cancelled the plan; all of it worked.

**What I tested on staging, each with a new test account:**
- **Credit pack, paid with Stripe's test card:** the page said "1,000 credits added" and the account showed 1,500. The checkout's return and Chargebee's webhook both reported the sale, and it counted once (500 plus a 500 launch bonus).
- **Hobby plan:** the page said "You're on Hobby", with 1,500 credits a month until 31 Jan, then 750. Billing and usage showed "Renews 10 Dec" and the Visa test card.
- **Obico Premium subscriber:** Credits and plans showed Hobby at $8 "With Obico Premium's 20% off", and Chargebee's cart applied the coupon for $8.00. I stopped there without paying.
- **Cancel:** the plan stopped renewing and stays until 10 Dec. The account reply sends no renewal date and an end date of 10 Dec, which the app's "Ends 10 Dec." line uses.
- **Errors:** Sentry shows no new errors since the deploy.

**A bug I found and fixed on the way.** Local development and staging share the test Chargebee site, and both named customers "jusprinv2-<user id>". User ids repeat across servers, so a staging account could have taken over a local test customer's saved card and subscription. A local test payment could also have added credits to an unrelated staging account. Staging now names its customers "jusprinv2-stg-<id>", and each server ignores the other's customers. Production and local development keep the old names.

The fix has a test that failed before the change and passes after. All 291 server tests pass. That run also replaced the earlier "287 pass", which I found had run on an incomplete copy of the code.

**Where things are:**
- **tsd-enterprise master (pushed):** three commits — the move to JusPrin's own Chargebee site (77fd19cadb), the billing fixes (2d97f4b1c7) and the customer-name fix (a72b271f7e). The release branch carries them as image obi.4104.
- **Staging:** all four deployments run obi.4104.
- **Ops repo:** the staging changes are committed locally as 1e6caf7 and not pushed. They sit on top of another session's unpushed commit, so pushing would send both.
- **Test site:** its webhook goes to app-stg.obico.io.
- **JusPrin app:** the "Ends 10 Dec." line is still only on the local branch claude/plan-ends-line.

**One harmless failure:** one webhook delivery failed once. Chargebee sent the event before its own lookup could return it, retried about 80 seconds later, and the retry succeeded.

**Production isn't ready.** It still runs obi.4098, the image from before this work. Releasing master to production before the following steps would break JusPrin 2's checkout there:
- You turn on JusPrin's live Chargebee site.
- Stripe and PayPal are connected to it, with PayPal's "Reference Transactions" setting checked.
- Production gets the live site's API key and its webhook.

The live site's look, its email sender and the JusPrin 1 coupons are also still open.

# JusPrin resources

This directory contains curated, production-facing JusPrin assets. Generated decks, PDFs, render trees, archives, inspection output, and design-tool working directories remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` and are indexed in `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md`.

- `branding/` contains the soft-serve mark in the gradient, ink and white.
- `ui/` contains the authoritative semantic product UI tokens, `design-tokens.json`, which the shell, the Agent page, and `tests/brand/` all read.
- `images/` contains the application icons the bundle and installer reference directly (`JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico`).
- `welcome/` contains the clip on the first-launch welcome screen, which Home's page bundles, and the credit its CC BY 2.0 photos require. The clip is a placeholder until a recording of the real app replaces it. It also holds Google's own "G" mark for the sign-in door's "Continue with Google" button, in Google's colours as its brand guidelines require; it is the one literal colour on the welcome.
- `startup/` contains the name animation in two versions, each light and dark: the nozzle prints the name one layer at a time and drops the dot on the i. The macOS splash plays `splash-name-*` over the lockup's name, in the box `component.splash.name*` in `ui/design-tokens.json`; it loops, starting as the name finishes, because the splash may be up for under a second. The About window plays `about-name-*` on every platform over the horizontal lockup's name, scaled down to the box `component.about.name*`; it prints once from an empty name and stops on the finished logo. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/splash_animation.py` draws it from the logo geometry; rerun it rather than editing the files.
- `overlay/images/` contains the splash, About and horizontal lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icon PNGs under OrcaSlicer's asset names; `Slic3r::var()` serves them in place of the stock files. They also cover `OrcaSlicer.svg` (message, release-note and update dialogs) and `OrcaSlicer-mac_256px.ico` (the Mac Dock icon while the app runs).

Every logo file (marks, lockups, overlays, app icons) is drawn by `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py` from one geometry: the cone, and the name in HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold cut into print layers. The output is flat paths with one linear gradient, so nanosvg renders it without masks or text elements. Change the logo there and rerun it; do not edit the generated files by hand, and do not stretch or recolor them.

:root {

  --action-disabled: #E4E0E6; --action-disabled-text: #8A838F;
  --status-success: #2D6A55; --status-danger: #B44757;
  --brand-orbit: #3A2D64; --brand-violet: #6F4F84; --brand-bloom: #CE84B7; --neutral-ink: #17131F;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --surface-canvas: #17131F; --surface-subtle: #211B2A; --surface-selected: #4B3E57;
    --text-primary: #F6F2F7; --text-secondary: #CFC5D3; --border-subtle: #4B3E57;
    --action-primary: #CE84B7; --action-primary-hover: #D99AC5; --action-on-primary: #17131F;
    --action-disabled: #342C3B; --action-disabled-text: #857B8C;
    --status-success: #4CAF82; --status-danger: #E07080;
  }
}
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
html, body { margin: 0; background: var(--surface-subtle); color: var(--text-primary);
  font: 14px/20px "HarmonyOS Sans SC", system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; }
main { max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 24px 16px 32px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px; }
h1, h2, h3, p { margin: 0; }
h1 { font-size: 24px; line-height: 30px; }
h2 { font-size: 18px; line-height: 24px; }
.small { font-size: 13px; line-height: 18px; }
.label { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; }
.secondary { color: var(--text-secondary); }
.bold { font-weight: 700; }
a { color: var(--action-primary); font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }
a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
form { margin: 0; }
.button { appearance: none; border: 0; margin: 0; font: inherit; font-size: 13px; line-height: 18px; cursor: pointer;
  display: inline-flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-height: 32px; padding: 6px 12px;
  border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-primary); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-subtle);
  text-decoration: none; font-weight: 400; white-space: nowrap; }
.button:hover { background: var(--surface-subtle); text-decoration: none; }
.button.primary { min-height: 34px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--action-primary);
  color: var(--action-on-primary); box-shadow: none; font-weight: 700; }
.button.primary:hover { background: var(--action-primary-hover); }
.button:disabled { cursor: default; background: transparent; color: var(--action-disabled-text); }
.button.wide { width: 100%; }
.card { background: var(--surface-canvas); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-subtle); padding: 24px; }
.note { padding: 12px 16px; background: var(--surface-selected); border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border-subtle);
  display: flex; gap: 16px; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.alert { color: var(--status-danger); }
.launch { position: relative; overflow: hidden; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding: 16px 24px; border-radius: 12px;
  background: linear-gradient(110deg, var(--brand-orbit) 0%, var(--brand-violet) 70%, var(--brand-bloom) 130%); color: #FFFFFF; }
.launch .kicker { font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--brand-bloom); }
.launch .sparkles { position: absolute; right: 24px; top: 8px; width: 160px; height: 64px; }
.launch .sparkles svg { position: absolute; display: block; fill: currentColor; }
.badge { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--brand-bloom);
  color: var(--neutral-ink); font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.badge svg { display: block; fill: currentColor; }
s { color: var(--text-secondary); font-weight: 400; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<main>
{% block content %}{% endblock %}
</main>
</body>
</html>

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`
@AGENTS.md

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.

```bash
cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Documentation

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Before designing a screen or writing any on-screen text, follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`: whole-screen boards with real strings, the wording rule, and a cold-reader check on screenshots before and after building.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
